title: Cerebral Cortex, Lateralization & Neuroplasticity
description: Master the four lobes of the cortex, split-brain research, language areas, and the brain's capacity to adapt.

slides.title: The Four Lobes of the Cortex 🧠
slides.content:
# The Cerebral Cortex

The wrinkled outer layer of the brain (cerebral cortex) handles advanced processing across four lobes:

* **Frontal Lobe**: Executive functions, decision-making, emotional regulation, planning, and voluntary movement (**Primary Motor Cortex**).
* **Parietal Lobe**: Processes tactile sensations—touch, temperature, pressure, pain (**Somatosensory Cortex**) and spatial awareness.
* **Occipital Lobe**: Houses the **Primary Visual Cortex** at the back of the skull; interprets shape, color, and motion.
* **Temporal Lobe**: Located by the ears; houses the **Primary Auditory Cortex**, facial recognition centers (fusiform face area), and language comprehension.

quizData.question: A patient suffering trauma to the back of the head experiences temporary blindness despite undamaged eyes. Which lobe was injured?
quizData.explanation: The occipital lobe at the rear of the skull contains the visual cortex responsible for decoding visual sensory input.

slides.title: Language Specialization: Broca vs. Wernicke 🗣️
slides.content:
## Specialized Cortical Language Regions

In most individuals, language centers reside predominantly in the **left hemisphere**:

* **Broca's Area** (Frontal Lobe, Left Hemisphere): Controls motor speech production.
  * *Broca's Aphasia*: Patient understands spoken words clearly but struggles intensely to articulate words ('broken speech').
* **Wernicke's Area** (Temporal Lobe, Left Hemisphere): Governs language comprehension.
  * *Wernicke's Aphasia*: Patient produces fluent, grammatically flowing sentences that are completely nonsensical ('word salad') and cannot understand spoken speech.

slides.title: Split-Brain Research & Lateralization ✂️
slides.content:
## Severing the Corpus Callosum

The **Corpus Callosum** is a thick band of axon fibers connecting the left and right cerebral hemispheres.

In pioneering work by **Roger Sperry** and **Michael Gazzaniga**, severe epileptic patients had their corpus callosum surgically severed ('split-brain' patients):
* An image flashed to the **right visual field** goes to the left hemisphere -> The patient can immediately verbalize what they saw.
* An image flashed to the **left visual field** goes to the right hemisphere -> The patient cannot say what they saw, but their left hand can easily draw or pick up the object!

slides.title: Neuroplasticity & The Endocrine System 🌱
slides.content:
## Brain Adaptability & Hormonal Control

* **Neuroplasticity**: The brain's lifelong ability to reorganize neural pathways in response to experience, learning, or brain damage. Younger brains possess significantly higher plasticity.
* **The Endocrine System**: Glandular communication network utilizing **hormones** secreted into the bloodstream.
  * **Pituitary Gland**: The 'master gland' controlled by the hypothalamus; orchestrates human growth and triggers other glands.
  * **Adrenal Glands**: Release adrenaline (epinephrine) and cortisol during physiological stress.

quizData.question: A split-brain patient is briefly shown a picture of a spoon in their LEFT visual field only. What will occur when asked what they saw?

options.text: They will verbally say 'I saw a spoon' without hesitation
They will verbally state they saw nothing, yet can pick up the spoon with their left hand
They will draw a fork with their right hand

quizData.explanation: Left visual field goes to the non-verbal right hemisphere; the right hemisphere controls the left hand, so the hand can locate the object even if the verbal left hemisphere saw nothing.
